mentl/aa3b043:
`mentl query <file> "imports"` answers every import edge in the weave with
whether the imported module brings any name the importing one references.
Every term was already in the graph: module_cells gives each module its
path, span and decls; an ImportStmt among those decls is the edge;
graph_refs_at answers each declared name's sites in O(refs). So the read is
a fold over edges, not a scan of text.

That distinction is the point. It reports 63 dead of 256 on the wheel,
where a shell census of the same question found 52 — a grep cannot tell a
used name from one written in a comment, and that gap is how three dead
`import types` lines sat unseen long enough to put the compiler's whole op
vocabulary into every user program.

module_cells returned (path, span) and dropped the cell's own decls, so
every consumer wanting a module's content re-derived it from text. It
carries the decls now.

The honest limit is stated at the site: imports are transitive, so an edge
bringing no referenced name of its own may still be the conduit by which a
third module arrives. The facet reports the direct reference it measured
and nothing about the conduit; Hβ.driver.link-is-reachability decides
those. The 63 are a reading, not a delete list.

Four ratchets tripped and three were fixed rather than raised. The ref
markers came off the new fns — the quiet gate is right that annotating
around inference is the inference failing, and they were written by copying
surrounding style. The two returned lambdas became hole-products under the
Stage Law, which left the anonymity tier nothing to convict. Backticked
names that resolved nowhere became prose. Only movers rose, by one.

Root cause of the $unify call stack exhaustion: $graph_chase_loop
was Tier-3 base — it returned NBound(TVar(next)) as-is without
following the inner TVar handle. When two handles were bound to
TVar(each_other), $unify dispatched endlessly:

  unify(A,B) → chase both → both NBound → extract TVar(B), TVar(A)
  → unify_types → both TVar → unify(B,A) → ... infinite loop

Fix: upgrade $graph_chase_loop to canonical form per src/graph.nx:269-272
chase_node. When NBound payload is TVar(next), follow transitively with
depth+1. Non-TVar payloads (TFun, TInt, TList, etc.) return immediately.
Depth bound at 100 remains as the cycle safety net.

bind h_fn to TList(TVar(h_q)) instead of bare TVar(h_q), so chase
stops at NBound(TList(...)) and generalize correctly enters the
